text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan says Kuwait is considering to subsidise private sector jobs for Kuwaitis. The state is studying ways to encourage nationals to take private sector jobs. About 98 percent of the national workforce is hired by the state which offers higher wages and guarantees job security.
- Ten Iraqi infiltrators arrested after crossing Kuwait's border with Iraq.
- International Committee of the Red Cross reiterates pledge to seek a solution to the issue of about 600 Kuwaitis believed to be detained in Iraq since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.

- Sri Lanka's President Chandrika Kumaratunga says her country is looking forward to recieve Kuwaiti investmnets. Kumaratunga left Kuwait on Wednesday after a three-day official visit to the Gulf Arab state.
- Kuwait to host an international fair for tourism and property starting today (Thursday).
- Gulf Arab states move to postpone Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit that Qatar plans to host in November.
- Kuwait not to face power shortage in summer, officials at the Ministry of Electricity and Water say.
- Trade union official says the Ministry of Health should meet the demands of workers so health services could be improved.
